interest: This file offers historians exceptional insight into the financial mechanics and intelligence dimensions of economic warfare during the breakdown of U.S.-Japanese relations in 1941 and the subsequent planning for Japan's postwar occupation. The July 1941 intelligence reports vividly capture the covert scramble by Japanese banks (Yokohama Specie Bank and Sumitomo Bank) on the eve of President Roosevelt's freezing order, detailing armored car transfers to smuggle $5,000,000 in bonds aboard the S.S. Tatuta Maru and emergency pre-freeze cash withdrawals in Honolulu. Furthermore, the October 1941 conference records document the delicate jurisdictional conflict between New York State banking regulators protecting domestic creditors and Federal officials seeking to avoid Japanese sovereign debt default via proposed gold imports or Federal Loan Agency bailouts of blocked silk acceptances. Finally, the 1944 military currency memorandum provides a fascinating look at early Allied occupation doctrine, illustrating how economic missteps and wage inflation in occupied Italy directly informed the design, denominations, and symbolic motifs of Allied Military Yen.
overview: This file comprises State Department memoranda, inter-agency conference minutes, FBI intelligence bulletins, diplomatic cross-reference sheets, and corporate correspondence spanning June 1941 to March 1944 under decimal file 894.516 (Japanese banking, credits, and public securities). The pre-Pearl Harbor documentation (June–October 1941) details the acute financial friction and regulatory fallout caused by the July 1941 executive order freezing Japanese assets in the United States, including pre-freeze runs and large cash withdrawals in Honolulu, covert attempts by the Yokohama Specie Bank in San Francisco to evacuate $5,000,000 in bonds and institutional records aboard the S.S. Tatuta Maru, corporate inquiries regarding the status of the National City Bank branch in Tokyo, and high-level State-Treasury deliberations over the impending insolvency of the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York agency due to halted bilateral trade, unliquidated silk acceptances, and obligations to service Japanese sovereign and corporate debt. The wartime records (1942–1944) shift to British intelligence monitoring Japanese capital movements in Latin America and currency exploitation in the occupied Netherlands East Indies, culminating in detailed inter-divisional planning for the design, denominations, and inflationary safeguards of Allied Military Yen ('Military Government Currency') for the occupation of Japanese territories.

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum analyzing the dwindling dollar liquidity of the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York agency and outlining potential policy remedies.
subfiles.from: George F. Luthringer and James (Division of Far Eastern Affairs / Office of Economic Adviser, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Reviews the critical depletion of dollar reserves at the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York agency caused by the complete cessation of U.S.-Japan bilateral trade following executive freezing orders. Examines potential policy measures to maintain Japanese debt service ($1,400,000 monthly) and official establishments ($200,000 monthly), including accepting Japanese gold shipments of $1,600,000 monthly or having the Federal Loan Agency purchase $19,000,000 in blocked raw silk bills receivable. Recommends endorsing a preliminary approach proposed by New York State banking authorities and preparing departmental strategy ahead of an inter-agency Treasury Policy Committee meeting.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Assistant Secretary Acheson on the Financial Position of the Yokohama Specie Bank New York Agency

subfiles.about: Record of an inter-agency conference at the Treasury Department reviewing regulatory options and creditor protection concerning the Yokohama Specie Bank in New York.
subfiles.from: Inter-agency Conference Participants (Treasury, State, Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York State Banking Department, National Bank Examiner)
subfiles.summary: Minutes of a conference held in Bernard Bernstein's Treasury office with officials from State, Treasury, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, the National Bank Examiner, and the New York State Banking Department to address the Yokohama Specie Bank's looming insolvency. State examiners found the branch possessed $8,300,000 in cash against $9,200,000 in liabilities, in addition to $19,000,000 in doubtful silk receivables subject to OPM controls. William R. White suggested courses of action including monitoring license authorizations, establishing an escrow account to shield domestic creditors, or forcing immediate liquidation. The conference also evaluated whether the bank could replenish dollar assets through transfers from South America, Hawaii, the Philippines, or gold exports from Japan.
subfiles.title: Conference Memorandum with Respect to New York Branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram regarding substantial fund payments from the Java Bank to the Yokohama Specie Bank in New York.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 60 from Consul General Walter A. Foote in Batavia, originally filed under 856d.5151/27. The communication reported that large sums transferred by the Java Bank to the New York agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank represented Japan's accrued bilateral trade balance in the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Telegram No. 60 from Batavia Concerning Java Bank Remittances to Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: Corporate inquiry regarding whether Japanese retaliatory freezing decrees affected the National City Bank branch in Tokyo and disrupted company finances.
subfiles.from: F. S. Thomas (Westinghouse Air Brake Company, Wilmerding, Pa.)
subfiles.summary: An executive of the Westinghouse Air Brake Company inquires about the operational and legal status of the National City Bank of New York's branch in Tokyo following the Japanese Government's retaliatory freezing regulations. The company relied on this branch to pay its local office expenses in Japan and notes that commercial mail contact with its Tokyo office had been completely cut off for more than two months.
subfiles.title: Letter from Westinghouse Air Brake Company Inquiring About the Status of National City Bank in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Westinghouse Air Brake Company's letter under frozen credits classification.
subfiles.from: F. S. Thomas (Westinghouse Air Brake Company)
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet indexing the August 22, 1941 letter from the Westinghouse Air Brake Company to decimal classification 840.51 (Frozen Credits). It summarizes the company's inquiry concerning the effect of Japanese freezing regulations on the National City Bank in Tokyo and the payment of corporate expenses.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Westinghouse Air Brake Company Letter on National City Bank in Tokyo

subfiles.about: State Department reply advising Westinghouse Air Brake Company to contact the New York headquarters of National City Bank for operational details on Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Herbert Feis (Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Official reply from Herbert Feis to F. S. Thomas of the Westinghouse Air Brake Company regarding the status of the National City Bank branch in Tokyo. Feis states that the National City Bank of New York is kept currently informed regarding the position of its Tokyo office under Japanese financial restrictions and recommends that the firm communicate directly with the bank's New York headquarters.
subfiles.title: Letter from Herbert Feis to Westinghouse Air Brake Company Regarding National City Bank in Tokyo
subfiles.to: F. S. Thomas (Westinghouse Air Brake Company)

subfiles.about: Confidential intelligence report detailing attempts by the Yokohama Specie Bank's San Francisco branch to evacuate $5,000,000 in bonds and bank records on the S.S. Tatuta Maru.
subfiles.from: Frederick B. Lyon (Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Confidential memorandum alerting senior State Department officials that S. Uno, Assistant Manager of the Yokohama Specie Bank in San Francisco, arranged with an armored car company to transport $5,000,000 in bonds to the Japanese vessel S.S. Tatuta Maru prior to its scheduled July 31 departure. The memorandum also reports that the bank engaged the Japanese Transfer Company to remove institutional records for shipment to Japan. Lyon requests instructions to convey to the FBI regarding countermeasures.
subfiles.title: Confidential Memorandum from Frederick B. Lyon Concerning Japanese Attempts to Transfer Bonds and Bank Records
subfiles.to: Sumner Welles, Adolf A. Berle, Jr., and Stanley K. Hornbeck

subfiles.about: Intelligence report on exceptional pre-freezing cash withdrawals by Japanese banks from the Bank of Hawaii in Honolulu.
subfiles.from: Frederick B. Lyon (Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Relays urgent telephone intelligence from the FBI Honolulu office regarding substantial cash withdrawals from the Bank of Hawaii immediately prior to President Roosevelt's public announcement freezing Japanese assets. The Yokohama Specie Bank withdrew $200,000 and the Sumitomo Bank withdrew $100,000, reportedly to satisfy anticipated depositor runs before accounts were frozen.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Frederick B. Lyon on Pre-Freezing Cash Withdrawals in Honolulu
subfiles.to: Sumner Welles, Stanley K. Hornbeck, Maxwell M. Hamilton, and Herbert Feis

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing British intelligence on the transfer of Japanese Mitsui Bank funds from Uruguay to Peru.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet indexing information furnished by the British Embassy concerning the transfer of funds belonging to Mitsui Bank (Tokyo) from Montevideo, Uruguay, to the Banco Italiano in Lima, Peru. Directs researchers to decimal file 865.516/212 for the underlying intelligence on Japanese financial diversions in Latin America.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: British Information on Transfer of Mitsui Bank Funds from Montevideo to Lima

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a British economic warfare despatch on Japanese currency devaluation in the occupied Dutch East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 6026 from Great Britain (Somerville), filed originally under 856d.515/35. The despatch incorporates economic warfare intelligence analyzing currency devaluation in the occupied Netherlands East Indies and evaluates the broader monetary and banking policies enforced by the Japanese military administration.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: British Despatch on Devaluation of Dutch East Indies Currency
subfiles.to: Department of State / British Foreign Office

subfiles.about: Inter-divisional policy memorandum outlining design guidelines, linguistic specifications, and denomination choices for Allied Military Yen currency.
subfiles.from: Abbot Low Moffat (Division of Liberated Areas, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Records State Department consensus regarding the design and denomination structure of Allied 'Military Government Currency' (military yen) for planned operations in the Pacific. Specifies neutral background ornamentation (approving bamboo motifs while rejecting cherry blossoms) and requires bilingual inscriptions in English and formal Japanese ideographs (kanji). Strongly urges printing large volumes of small fractional notes (10 and 50 sen) to prevent wage inflation, citing adverse lessons learned from Allied overpayment of laborers during the occupation of Italy, while recommending against printing 5 sen and 200 yen denominations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Abbot Low Moffat Concerning Basic Designs and Denominations for Military Yen
subfiles.to: Jacques J. Reinstein (Division of Liberated Areas, Department of State)
